F1: Google passes the whole `safeParse` result (`{success, data}`) to `credential.key` at line 100, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse` fails.
F2: refreshOAuthTokens` gets `credentialId` (`credential.id`) as the user ID, so sync mode asks for tokens for the wrong user and team credentials also take the sync path.
F3: The computed keys both become `"[object Object]"`, so it doesn't fail every response, but zod still strips `expires_in`/`refresh_token`; Zoom then saves a NaN expiry and Office keeps a stale expiry in sync mode.
F4: In sync mode the callers get a fetch `Response`, so Google, Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `.data` (undefined) and HubSpot saves NaN/undefined token fields; the error is either swallowed or thrown.
F5: prisma` is never imported; TypeScript won't complain because a global is declared, but `globalThis.prisma` is only set outside production, so production throws a ReferenceError.
F6: Node fetch over HTTP/1.1 sets `statusText` to "OK", and the dead branch causes no wrong behavior.
F7: Refreshing on every construction costs speed and is a design choice, but it isn't a correctness defect.
F8: The literal `"refresh_token"` is written over the stored refresh token (always in sync mode, because the schema strips the field), which corrupts the credential.
F9: The Zoom app's slug is `zoom`, so sending `"zoomvideo"` to the sync endpoint doesn't match the slug the webhook and the app use.
F10: A timing attack on a network string compare is hardening, and an array header just fails the check.
F11: Returning 500 instead of 400 on a malformed webhook body is low value; nothing breaks.
F12: The payload comes from a trusted, secret-authenticated source and is validated when read, so write-time validation is only hardening.
F13: The sync endpoint is left for the operator to define (the code says to customize the payload), so outbound auth is a design suggestion, not a defect.
